The #1588 dogfood re-run measured warm autonomous recall at ~4.0 s on a long-content corpus vs ~0.5 s on short rows — the candle CPU forward was the cost. **[TRUTH-FIX #2576, v1.0.0]** the original rationale here was wrong in two ways, and both mattered because they invited a default retune that would have silently degraded relevance. (1) It said long-content rows "pad the whole batch to 512 tokens". They do not: `neural_score_pairs` sets `tokenizers::PaddingStrategy::BatchLongest`, so the batch is padded to the longest sequence PRESENT IN THAT BATCH, never to `max_seq`. `max_seq` is a **TRUNCATION** bound, not a pad width — it only binds when a pair actually tokenizes longer than the cap, and when it binds it DISCARDS document tokens the cross-encoder would otherwise have scored. (2) It said "BERT attention is O(n²) in sequence length, so the 256 default cuts the forward ~4×". At these lengths the 1536-d FFN dominates and attention is ~10% of the MACs, so the forward is ~LINEAR in L: a measured 142→64 (2.2× shorter) gave 2.0× faster, not 4.8×. Measured consequence on the #2576 reference corpus (7,855 Atlas rows, content avg 391 B / p50 378 / p95 593 / max 940): at `max_seq=256` **0.0%** of (query, doc) pairs are truncated and the batch pads to ~135 tokens — **the 256 default costs nothing on this corpus**. At `max_seq=64`, **91.8%** of pairs truncate and the median document loses ~28% of its tokens. #2576 proposed 256→64 for a measured ~30% latency win; the 5-agent vote (`4d3ea1c5`) REFUSED it 5/5 because that win is bought by deleting the document, and a compiled default is a fleet-wide contract. Pinned by `tests/rerank_cross_encoder_gate_2576.rs::rerank_max_seq_default_stays_256_2576`; do not retune without a measured relevance A/B. Resolves through `AppConfig::resolve_reranker()` (env > `[reranker].max_seq_tokens` > compiled default) and is seeded process-wide at boot via `crate::reranker::set_rerank_max_seq`. Zero / unparseable / above-ceiling values fall through. Source: `crate::config::ENV_RERANK_MAX_SEQ`. |
